summary: Kootenai County lookout at 5,199 ft: a 1934 pole tower, replaced in 1963 by a 53-foot tower that was torn down about 1998. No source describes the summit today.

facts.status_note: Torn down about 1998; no source describes what remains
facts.agency: Idaho Department of Lands (operation from 1966); land also listed as Coeur d'Alene National Forest and Coeur d'Alene Indian Reservation

corrections.proposed: 53-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab (1963)
corrections.why: The L-4 cab belonged to the 1934 pole tower; the tower standing from 1963 until it was torn down about 1998 had an R-6 flat cab
The 1963 tower was 53 feet, about 16.2 m; 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height of the 1934 pole tower
Both sites say the tower was torn down about 1998; neither says it was destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's L-4 cab and 15.2 m height describe the first 1934 tower. The 1963 replacement was 53 feet with an R-6 cab and stood until about 1998, so both descriptions fit different periods.

notes_for_editor: Structure history is well corroborated across three sites. Disputes left open: Grorud (1971) calls the tower 60 feet, against 53 feet in the other sources; last use is 1970s on firelookout.com and 1970? on Idaho Fire Lookouts, with abandonment in the 1980s on Forest Lookouts. Staff names come from two sites, several attributed to the Kellogg Evening News; newspapers not checked. Forest Lookouts' 'TFA' label is unexplained and not used. Idaho Fire Lookouts' 2016 entry is for Eagle Mountain, a different lookout, and was ignored. Record corrections (design, height_m, 1998 event) are already reflected in facts and events; the corrections list is kept for human review. No source found on remains or public access. Fact check 2026-10-10: the firelookout.com staff list has 19 named entries, nine of them couples (1947, 1948, 1951, 1952, 1953, 1954, 1955, 1957, 1967), with gaps between entries, so year by year was dropped from the story. The Grorud access and smoke account is paraphrased in the story.
